Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing follow-up - FinTechCo

Hi Samantha -

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can size Dedicated capacity correctly:

Summary of what you shared
- Primary use case: customer-facing chat + document summarization (support & KYC flows).
- Current production traffic: growing with marketing campaign; baseline traffic relatively low but spiky.
- Deployment preference: leaning toward Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) with a plan to evaluate Private VPC for later projects.

Sizing questions we still need from you (short answers or a CSV will do):
1) Target TPS / requests per second (avg and peak): what do you expect in normal hours vs peak events?
2) Concurrent sessions/users expected at peak.
3) Token mix: average prompt tokens, average response tokens, and any max token limits.
4) Model family / latency expectations (p95 target), and whether you need streaming.
5) Any preference on GPU class (NVIDIA H100 vs A100 / 80GB vs 40GB) or constraints from your infra team.
6) Embeddings or batch rerank workloads (approx % of requests).

I attached the sizing deck and a template CSV you can paste actual traffic into - I filled a couple of example rows from the call.

Next steps
- If you can send answers to the questions above, we'll produce a recommended node layout (GPUs per node, nodes required for baseline + 2x spike buffer), estimated throughput, and a cost projection.
- Optionally schedule a short throughput validation run (15-130m) once we have credentials/whitelisted IPs.

Happy to hop on a 20-min follow-up if that's easier.

Thanks -
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rafael@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Thanks Rafael - appreciate the clear list. Answers below (copied our infra lead on a couple of items):

1) TPS / RPS\- Typical: 10-15 req/s\- Peak (marketing spikes / payroll day): up to ~35 req/s for short windows (5-10 min)
2) Concurrency\- We expect ~60 concurrent sessions at peak across web + mobile; many are short chat exchanges but some heavy docs are longer-running.
3) Token mix\- Avg prompt: ~180 tokens\- Avg response: ~220 tokens\- Max request (rare): ~2,048 tokens
4) Model & latency\- We'd like p95 <= 300ms for chat generation (non-streamed acceptable), and streaming would be nice for the live chat experience.
5) GPU preference\- Our infra team prefers H100s where available; A100 80GB is acceptable as fallback. Cost sensitivity: we want a balance between latency and cost.
6) Embeddings / batch jobs\- Embeddings are used for retrieval in ~18% of requests; nightly batch rerank jobs run for smaller subsets (noisy, low qps).

I attached a short traffic snapshot (prod_traffic_snapshot.csv) for the last 7 days. Let us know if you want anything else.

Samantha Chen
Head of Product - FinTechCo
samantha@fintechco.com

Great - thanks for the details and for the snapshot, Samantha. Based on the numbers you provided, initial sizing notes below (high level):

Assumptions used
- Model: open-chat-7B equivalent (production-quality generation with quantization); we can model the same for Llama-family or a larger 13B if you prefer.
- Avg tokens per req: 400 (prompt + response)
- Target p95 latency: <=300ms (non-streaming), streaming optional with slightly higher resource needs

Preliminary recommended layout
- Node type: 1-2 H100 80GB GPUs per node (preferred) OR 2 x A100 80GB as fallback
- Baseline capacity: 3 nodes (2 GPUs each) to comfortably cover 10-15 req/s with headroom for model kv cache and autoscaling
- Spike buffer / reserved headroom: additional capacity to absorb short peaks up to 35 req/s - recommend either 2 spare nodes in the Dedicated pool or a burst policy to spin additional nodes for 5-10m windows
- Concurrency: we expect 60 concurrent sessions to be handled across the pool; autoscaling and request routing will keep p95 targets.

Estimated throughput (very rough)
- With the above layout and model selection, we estimate sustained 12-15 req/s with p95 ~250-350ms; burst to 30-35 req/s would increase p95 to ~400ms unless additional burst nodes are available.

Next steps
1) We can run a brief throughput validation run (we'll need ephemeral API keys + whitelisted IPs). This will validate token mix and real p95 numbers with your payloads.
2) If the test is acceptable, we'll provide a firm node-count and cost estimate and draft a Reserved Capacity agreement.
3) Marissa - can you prepare a draft SOW and pricing for a 6-month Reserved Capacity + burst option?

I'll schedule 30m next week for the throughput run unless you prefer to coordinate a different cadence.

Thanks,
Rafael
